title: Distribution Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
2.     MOS 3152, Distribution Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Distribution Specialists are educated, equipped, and
trained to manage fleet marine force requirements at the tactical,
operational, strategic, and enterprise level. The specialists use Federal,
DoD, and service regulations, the defense transportation system (DTS),
commercial modes of transportation, and distribution logistic functions to
enable optimal selection and procurement of commercial and government-
operated land, air, and sea transportation services. They use a variety of
automated systems in the performance of their duties. Warehousing, rail,
motor and air terminal operations, materiel handling, packing, packaging,
preservation, and marking are daily operations. Distribution Specialists
perform technical distribution management duties pertaining to movement of
civilian and military personnel and their eligible family members both
individually and in groups, using all modes of transportation. This includes
planning for troop movements via chartered air, train, or bus, as well as
port calls for overseas permanent change of station. The specialists perform
personal property counseling interviews to advise members and eligible family
members of their personal property shipping entitlements. The specialists
perform additional operational duties and tasks at military and commercial
air terminals. The specialists perform passport and visa services by
counseling members and dependents on required documents, foreign clearance
regulations, and by aiding in the preparation and submission of required
correspondence to the Department of State and foreign embassies. This
includes preparing all freight shipment documents to manifest cargo and
passengers aboard government or commercial chartered conveyances. At the
operational level, specialists perform in-theater sustainment receiving,
shipping, in-transit visibility, and distribution functions.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must possess a GT score of 85 or higher.

             (2) Must have a valid civilian motor vehicle operator's license.

             (3) Security requirement:

                 (a) Secret security clearance eligibility (SSgt and above).

            (b) Must possess a favorably adjudicated national agency check
with local agency check and credit checks (NACLC) personnel security
investigation.




                                         3-270                        Enclosure (1)
 3126                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (4) No convictions by court-martial, civilian courts, or non-judicial
punishment of any act involving larceny or theft.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Distribution Specialist Basic Course
(M0368X1), MCCSSS, Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (t), Distribution Specialist Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Entry level Marines (Sgt to Pvt) holding entry level ranks
perform the duties and tasks comparable to the following classifications:

                (a) Logisticians 13-1081.

                (b) Financial Managers 11-3031.

                (c) Cargo and Freight Agent 43-5011.

                (d) Production, Planning and Expediting Clerks 43-5061.

        (2) Mid-level Management Marines (GySgt to SSgt) holding mid-level
management ranks perform the related duties from the entry level ranks with
the following additional classifications:

            (a) First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support
Workers 43-1011.

                (b) Business Operations Specialist 13-1199.

        (3) Senior-level Management Marines (MGySgt to MSgt) holding senior
level management ranks perform the related duties from the previous
classifications with the following classifications:

                (a) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

                (b) Purchasing Managers 11-3061.

                (c) Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

                (d) Management Analyst 13-1111.

                (e) Packers and Packagers, Hand 53-7064.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Logistics/Embarkation Specialist, 0431.

            (2) Logistics/Mobility Chief, 0491.

            (3) Enlisted Aviation Logistician, 6617.




                                        3-271                        Enclosure (1)
 3127                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
